about: Where each app draws its own interface over a vertical video, in pixels of a 1080x1920 frame. `covered` are rectangles measured on the mobile web versions (375x812 screen, 16 Nov 2026), scaled to the frame as if the video filled the screen: what was actually under buttons and text. `margins` and `column` ([from x, from y, to y]) are the published safe zones for ads, a stricter limit used with `margins: "ads"`. `top` is the room kept for the header the native apps draw and the web versions do not. `bottom` replaces the measurement where the web version cannot show it.

tiktok.source: TikTok Ads, In-Feed safe zone template

instagram.source: Meta Business Help Center, safe zone for ads in Stories and Reels (14% top, 35% bottom, 6% each side)

youtube.source: Google, YouTube Shorts ads (10% top, 25% bottom, 10% right)
youtube.note: On the mobile web the title and channel sit below the video, so the bottom could not be measured: the published margin is used.
